clue.text: Nowhere is perfect

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word was coined from Greek for 'no place'

definitions.note: adjective; the answer is the noun for a perfect place
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an ideal, flawless society

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a gloomy proverb, but it pairs the literal Greek sense of the word with its everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More coined the name from Greek roots meaning no place, and it now denotes an ideal imaginary society.

clue.text: Trials a holy man set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saintly figure arranges ordeals for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests and trials are both examinations that check how something or someone performs.

clue.text: Settle on woven cane maybe

indicators.note: weaving interlaces strands, so the letters of the following word are worked into a new order

parts.note: a bird will perch on, or settle on, a branch
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird alights on a piece of wickerwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned adverb with the same sense of possibility, like perhaps.

clue.text: Attachment for a girl over the water

parts.note: a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England; in a down clue the first piece sits over it

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of a girl living across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building or document added on to a main one, an attached extension.

clue.text: Money that is solely for material

parts.note: a common synonym
mere describes something that is solely what it is, nothing more

explanation.surface: Funds earmarked purely for buying fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric made from the hair of Kashmir goats.

clue.text: In a ship one goes up and down

definitions.text: In a ship one goes up and down

parts.words: In a ship one goes up and down
parts.note: surface reading: a sailor rising and falling on the waves
setter's reading: the thing itself is climbed up and down between decks

explanation.walkthrough: 'One' seems to be a person tossed on the swell; it is really a fixture that people climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion ladder is the steep stairway leading from a ship's deck down to the cabins below.

clue.text: Aplomb shown by 22 perhaps in accommodation fit only for pigs

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, sitting inside its letters
perhaps signals the name may appear in some other form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 22-down, the girl's name, with its letters rearranged
a sty is a pig's pen

explanation.surface: A woman keeps her composure despite living in a hovel.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference number stands for that clue's answer, here the girl's name at 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is calm self-possession, close to aplomb, which is poised confidence.

clue.text: The person with gold will get the property

parts.note: a person, a man
or is gold in heraldry; with means it is added

explanation.surface: Whoever has the money will end up owning the estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a landed estate with a large country house, a substantial piece of property.

clue.text: Down-to-earth military men in charge holding a schedule

indicators.note: holding means the outer letters surround and grip what follows

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
taken as written
a schedule is a list
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Practical soldiers who run things to a timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are the army's sappers, a frequent source of RE in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A realistic person is practical and sensible about what can be achieved, down-to-earth.

clue.text: Scientist rents a room for working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work and moved into a fresh order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A researcher takes lodgings to have somewhere to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars, planets and other bodies in space.

clue.text: Elegant beasts

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an old word for cattle

explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an archaic word for oxen and cows, a sense kept alive in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trim and smart, and also, in old usage, bovine cattle as a herd.

clue.text: Ending breathless

parts.note: surface reading: finishing a race or effort out of puff
setter's reading: dying from lack of air

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a runner gasping at the finish, but the ending is a fatal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphyxia is the condition of suffocation, when oxygen is cut off and death can result.

clue.text: Put detectives right on turning over Scandinavian

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so the string is read backwards

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to set police officers straight about something from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the peoples and countries of northern Europe, including Scandinavia.

clue.text: Start work in French

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the French word for in

explanation.surface: Beginning a job in the French language.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to begin it, as in opening a meeting or a campaign.

clue.text: Carry on quietly to rescue odd characters

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are treated as characters to be put in an unusual order

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quietly saves a group of eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute a war or campaign is to pursue it, keep it going, conduct it.

clue.text: Confidential hint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: private and personal, as an adjective
second meaning: to suggest indirectly, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one ends in -mut, the other in -mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for close and private, and a verb meaning to suggest or imply.

clue.text: Contrive to get at inside of engine

indicators.note: inside of means one word is placed within the letters of another

parts.note: an engine is a machine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mechanic works out how to reach the inner parts of a motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside of engine' looks like a phrase for the motor's innards, but it tells you where the little word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or plot, devising plans in a crafty way, much like contriving.

clue.text: Promise made by witches to a worker

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A coven of witches gives its word to a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a solemn agreement or binding pledge, a formal promise.

clue.text: Forsaken by sweetheart, desire to see service

parts.note: a synonym
lo is an old word meaning look or see
the Royal Navy, the senior service

explanation.surface: A jilted lover longs to join the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is traditionally called the senior service, so a service is often RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelorn describes someone pining because their love is unreturned or they have been abandoned.

clue.text: Get set to fire a male

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to raise the hammer of a gun ready for shooting
second meaning: a male bird, especially a rooster

explanation.surface: An order to shoot a man.
explanation.definitionFit: One cocks a gun by pulling back its hammer, and a cock is a male fowl.

clue.text: A statement about drink

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: An official account concerning alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a formal account or statement describing what happened.

clue.text: Punish repeatedly to bring about some improvement

parts.note: the prefix meaning again
to punish with a money penalty

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian keeps penalising people to make them better.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: punishing again is fining again.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to polish or purify it, making small improvements.

clue.text: She's in need of an entire new outfit

parts.note: surface padding

indicators.note: in means the name sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words
surface padding

explanation.surface: A woman needs a completely new set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue is surface dressing around the hidden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's name, so she is a fair way to point to it.

clue.text: Statesmanlike?

parts.note: surface reading: having the dignity of a senior politician
setter's reading: a man from the States, the USA

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the word is split: like a States man.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans come from the United States, often called simply the States.

clue.text: All that remained of a vessel carrying high explosive

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, like cargo in a hold

parts.note: SS is a steamship
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Only wreckage was left of a ship loaded with explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are the residue left after something has burnt away, all that remains of it.

clue.text: Score a point, being smart

parts.note: to score a surface is to cut a line in it
east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A player wins a point through cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean clever or shrewd, especially in American usage.

clue.text: A Trojan woman had no cream for cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman from Troy lacked an ingredient for her recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromache was Hector's wife in Homer's Iliad and a heroine of Euripides' play The Trojan Women.

clue.text: He leaves dry land with little hesitation

parts.note: an arid region
the short sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off across arid terrain without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter is someone who abandons a post or duty, especially a soldier who runs away.

clue.text: He believes he is entering the race

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these words are placed within the other piece

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
taken as written

explanation.surface: A competitor has faith he will make it into the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is a person who holds that God or gods exist, a believer.
